note: Golden retrieval set. Every expectedChunkId is a real id in content/dist/content.json and run.mjs refuses to run if one is not. A question is an ABSTENTION question when `expects` is "abstain", or — when `expects` is absent — when expectedChunkIds is empty. Abstention questions split three ways: out-of-corpus (not in the corpus at all), structured-only (in content.json as a structured field, but not as a chunk, so only the tool layer can answer it), and corpus-gap (an entity that exists but produced no chunk).
_expects: `expects` exists for the one question where the two definitions disagree — metric-token-count. Its expectedChunkIds are still the RIGHT passages and are kept, but after the design-system stats were decoupled neither of them contains the digits any more, so the answer lives only in get_system_facts. Deriving abstention from an empty array would have forced a choice between deleting correct ground truth and scoring a question retrieval cannot answer. run.mjs prints every question where the explicit flag overrides the derived one, so the exception is visible rather than silent.
_shape: `shape` records the FORM of the question, independently of its subject category. It was added because audit 05 §2.5 found the set tested lookup and almost nothing else: of the 54 questions in version 1, 52 were plain lookup and 2 were adversarial. The eleven questions added in version 2 carry the missing shapes — negation, comparative, multi-hop, temporal, and one more fabricated-employer probe. Shapes are reported with their n and a Wilson interval, because a shape bucket of 2 is a bucket of 2.
_version2: Version 2, written AFTER the entity gate was rebuilt (name/label split, IDF floor, proper-noun test). The eleven new questions are therefore the first in this set that the gate was not built against — a small held-out probe, not a held-out SET: they were written by an agent that had read gate.js, so they are out-of-sample for the gate's tuning and not for its author's knowledge. Two of the two queries quoted in gate.js's own header as design examples were deliberately NOT copied in. Two version-1 questions were reworded to remove wording that echoed their target heading (proj-spetema-ia, metric-deadlift); both still have the same expected chunks. No question was added, removed or reworded after seeing a result.

questions.question: What was the Domestina project about?
Who were the three user types on the Domestina marketplace?
How was the Spetema coffee site laid out so two very different kinds of buyer could each find their way?
questions.why: REWORDED in version 2. It read "How was the information architecture of the Spetema coffee site structured?" against a target chunk whose heading is literally "Information architecture" — audit 05 §2.5 flagged that it inflated BM25 and the gate together and tested no paraphrase. The expected chunk is unchanged; only the question wording moved, and it moved away from the heading, never toward it.

questions.question: Has he shipped anything that runs with no build step at all?
questions.why: NEW in version 2 — negation. "No build step in the site" and "pure static, no build" are the two passages; every other design-system passage in the corpus is about a build that DOES run, so polarity is the whole discriminator.

questions.question: Of everything he has worked on, which change produced the biggest measured improvement?
questions.why: NEW in version 2 — comparative. Answering it requires ordering numbers that live in different entities (40% bounce reduction, 200+ issue instances, ~35 components, 100% token coverage). No single chunk states the comparison, which is the point: a ranker can only surface the winning passage, never compute the ranking.

questions.question: Which of the projects from his studio years ended up live on both app stores?
questions.why: NEW in version 2 — multi-hop across two entities. Hop one: which projects belong to Studio Kipo. Hop two: which of those is on BOTH stores — Mindromeda is Google Play only, so a retriever that stops at 'app store' returns the wrong project.

questions.question: At the company where he redesigned an AI Assistant module, what accessibility work did he also do?
questions.why: NEW in version 2 — multi-hop across two entities. The employer is named nowhere in the question; it has to be resolved from 'AI Assistant module' (project:greenstreet-ds#problem) before the accessibility work can be found in a different project entirely.

questions.why: REWORDED in version 2. It read "What is his heaviest deadlift?" against a fact whose CV label is literally "Heaviest deadlift." — audit 05 §2.5 flagged the echo. The expected chunks are unchanged. The paraphrase is genuinely harder: the site label is "Heaviest lift", the CV label is "Heaviest deadlift", and `lift` is also a name token of experience:live-to-lift.

questions.question: How big was the coaching team he managed?
Which was bigger — the coffee catalogue or the trading platform's component set?
questions.why: NEW in version 2 — comparative across two entities. 200+ products against 50+ Figma components and variants; both numbers are in the corpus and the comparison is in neither chunk. Named `expectedEntity` is the winning side, which is the limitation of a single-entity ground truth on a comparative question and is recorded rather than hidden.

questions.question: Where is he based?
questions.why: profile.identity.location is a structured field. The only chunk containing the word 'Sofia' is profile:education (Sofia University), so lexical search answers this confidently and wrongly.

questions.question: Is he available for new work right now?
questions.why: profile.availability is a structured field. The only chunk matching 'available' is project:malko-tarnovo#outcome ('publicly available on both stores').

questions.question: What's his email address?
questions.why: profile.contact is a structured field. No chunk contains an email address.

questions.question: What was he doing in 2019?
questions.why: NEW in version 2 — temporal, and the shape turns out to be structured-only in this corpus. Employment dates live in experience[].period; the BM25 index contains NO four-digit year token at all, so no search over prose can answer a date question. Only list_experience can.

questions.question: How many tokens and components does this site's own design system have?
questions.why: RECATEGORISED in version 2 from `metric` to `structured-only`, by owner decision, with the reason on file. After the design-system statistics were decoupled from the prose, neither expected chunk contains the digits: project:portfolio-system#outcome now reads 'tokens, values, components' and profile:open-source reads 'tokens carrying values across light, dark & print · components'. The counts live only in content.json's system block, reachable only through get_system_facts. The expected chunks are KEPT because they are still the right passages — they are simply no longer the right ANSWER — so `expects` carries the abstention verdict explicitly instead of it being inferred from an emptied array.

questions.question: Did he ever work in quality assurance?
questions.why: The 2007-2009 QA role at CNCsys PLC has no bullets, so build-content.mjs produced no chunk for it. It exists in content.json's experience array and nowhere in chunks.

questions.question: What did he do at CNCsys?
questions.why: NEW in version 2 — grows a bucket audit 05 flagged at n=1. This is the sharpest corpus-gap shape: the query names a real entity by its own id, so the entity gate is RIGHT to report coverage, and the corpus still has nothing to return. Coverage and content disagree, and only this question shows it.

questions.question: What was his first technical job before he moved into design?
questions.why: NEW in version 2 — grows the corpus-gap bucket, and adds a temporal shape whose answer is a role rather than a date. The CNCsys descriptor says 'first technical role' in as many words, and descriptors are not chunked, so the sentence that answers this exists in content.json and in no chunk.

questions.question: Does he have experience with Kubernetes or backend infrastructure?
What are his salary expectations?
Did he ever work at Google?
questions.why: 'Google' appears eight times in the corpus — Google Analytics, Google Play, Google AI Studio — none of them an employer.

questions.question: Does he speak Japanese?
Has he built anything in Unity or Unreal?
questions.why: 'Unity' matches 'community' inside two chunks after tokenisation only if substring-matched; as a whole token it does not occur. A good check that the retriever is not substring-matching.

questions.question: Has he published a book or spoken at conferences?
Does he hold a Nielsen Norman Group certification?
Was he a product designer at Hotjar?
questions.why: NEW in version 2 — the fabricated-employer shape from audit 03's C2, which the version-1 set tested exactly once (oob-google). 'Hotjar' appears in four chunks as a research TOOL and never as an employer, while 'product' and 'designer' are labels five roles share. gate.js's header quotes two queries that were used to DESIGN the name/label split; neither was copied here, because measuring a gate against the examples it was built from is the §2.3 error repeated.
